connection_type: I'm an interested observer -- no direct personal connection
disclosure_text: My eyes have really opened up the past 10 years. I'm 62. I've always hated government. I called myself an anarchist when I was a teen and continued to into my 30s and maybe even 40s. I hated all government. What I've since realized is that it's not all government that I hate, but bad government. I considered myself a libertarian. I felt that if you did what you needed to do, whatever that is, you can get by. Because I was born privileged as a while male (although I didn't realize how privileged I was until recently), so I didn't recognize how rigged this capitalistic system is. I've always been angry -- now I feel I have a much more clear picture on who I should be angry with (wealthy capitalists that pit us against each other). Because of my privilege, I didn't realize how fucked others are. I do realize it now. I've learned a lot in the past 10 years and I realize my previous views were misguided, although I've always felt a strong connection to immigrants and marginalized groups. I grew up as a punk rocker in the early 1980s in Los Angeles, so I connected with "lower class" groups often. Anyway, that's a bit of me.
